leaderboard.formula: Skill = sum of (market Brier minus own Brier) / (questions with a baseline + 20), in points (x 100). Positive means better than the market.

crowd.title: Agent ID Crowd
crowd.intro: The Agent ID Crowd combines every revealed forecast into one probability per question. Each Agent ID belongs to one verified person and cannot be transferred, so the crowd resists fake accounts.
crowd.methodTitle: Method v1 (pre registered 23 Nov 2026, before any mainnet round)
method: Weights: equal weight for anyone with fewer than 3 resolved rounds. After that, 0.1 plus max(0, shrunk skill) divided by the average skill of established forecasters (shrinkage K = 20). Only rounds resolved before this round's commit deadline count, so nothing leaks from the future.
Combination: each forecast is clamped to 1% to 99% and averaged with these weights in log odds space. No extremizing in v1; adding it would need a new pre registered version.
The crowd, the simple mean and the market are always scored side by side with the same Brier rule over the same questions. Nothing is swapped after the fact.
Anyone can recompute every aggregate from chain data and the published snapshots.
crowd.honesty: The site always shows whether the crowd beats the market, even when it does not.
crowd.waiting: Waiting for results: scored once its questions settle onchain

profile.title: Profiles
body: Profiles appear only for forecasters who opt in, or for your own address.

Each profile will show a reliability diagram with 10 bins and the diagonal reference, skill over time, a breakdown by category, your streak, and your full forecast history with links to every transaction.
There is no search by name for people who have not opted in.

docs.title: Docs
docs.intro: How Forewit works, how it scores, and what its owner can and cannot do.

how.title: How it works
blocks: Two ways to forecast, one track record:

list: Any market, any time: give your chance on any yes or no market on Predict.fun. The market price at your commit is posted onchain within 2 minutes, and you are scored against it when the market settles.
The daily round: a few featured questions each day with a fixed deadline. The market price just before the deadline is the baseline.

blocks: Your forecast stays sealed, so nobody can copy it. With auto reveal on, Forewit opens it for you after the deadline or when the market ends, so there is no second step.
Scores are tied to your Agent ID. An Agent ID cannot be transferred and there is one per Binance user, so a track record cannot be bought, sold or faked with many wallets.
The Agent ID Crowd combines all revealed forecasts into one forecast per question, and the site shows whether it beats the market.

list: Brier score: (your chance minus what happened) squared, from 0 (perfect) to 1 (fully wrong). Lower is better.
Skill: the market's Brier minus yours. Above 0 means you were closer to the truth than the market.
A forecast that is never revealed counts as the worst possible score. Revealing is never worse.
Void questions (an unclear or early resolution) are skipped for everyone.
Not counted: a forecast with no reliable market price at its commit (the market's last 60 seconds, under 100 USD traded in 24 hours, or right after a price jump).
Score = total skill / (questions with a market price + 20). The 20 keeps a lucky few questions from topping the board.
You are ranked after 5 scoring days and 20 questions with a market price, daily rounds and any market forecasts together.
Rank uses skill against the market, never raw Brier.

selection.title: Question selection
blocks: Rule v3.1, pre registered on 23 Nov 2026. No sports and no politics questions. The keeper applies it mechanically and archives its output plus a fingerprint of the market list it read (the list itself stays private under Predict.fun's terms), so anyone can rerun it with their own key. A round never changes rules after it opens.

list: Binary and unresolved on one of the allowlisted Conditional Tokens contracts, with Yes as the first outcome.
No sports or esports markets.
Every non crypto question needs a two sided order book, a spread of at most 10 points and at least 100 USD of 24 hour volume.
At most one market per event.
Daily rounds: the daily crypto Up or Down markets plus liquid event markets, ending 6 to 72 hours after the commit deadline, 3 to 8 questions, resolution wait 7 days.
Long horizon rounds: liquid event markets ending more than 72 hours and at most 100 days after the deadline, resolution wait 120 days.

blocks: Every question is shown with its parent event question and its option, for example the event "Highest temperature in Shenzhen on November 24?" with the option "24°C". A question without an event question is never shown.

owner.title: Safety and owner permissions
blocks: All four contracts (ForecastLedger, OpenForecasts, ForewitScores, ForewitStart) cannot be upgraded, hold no funds and ask for no approvals. ForewitStart has no owner at all. Every transaction you send has value 0.

list: edit or delete forecasts, reveals, outcomes or scores;
set a market outcome (outcomes come only from the Conditional Tokens payouts onchain, or Void);
move any asset, because the contracts hold none.

blocks.h: What the operator roles can do

list: Daily round (ForecastLedger): create rounds by the published selection rule, post the market baseline once in the last 15 minutes before the deadline, and pause new commits. Pause never blocks reveal or scoring.
Any market (OpenForecasts): post the market price once, or void a forecast, only within 120 seconds of its commit; pause new commits only.
Free start (ForewitStart): no roles at all; nobody can change or stop it.
Admin: grant and revoke roles. Moving the admin seat takes two steps with a 1 day delay.
Sealed: nobody can read a forecast before its deadline, so nobody can copy it.
Scored against the market: copying the market price scores about zero skill.
One Agent ID per person, so nobody can fake a record with many wallets.
Market titles and all API text are treated as data, never as instructions.
This site is read only: no wallet connection and no secrets.

blocks: Independent reviews of the mainnet contracts found no open High or Medium issue. The full owner permissions, security reviews and threat model are in the GitBook docs.
Found a security problem? Report it privately through GitHub security advisories on the forewit repository.

blocks.strong: Forecasting scores only. Not financial advice. Forewit does not take bets, hold funds or pay returns. Prediction markets and crypto are risky and may be restricted in your region.

list: Forewit records forecasts and scores. It is not a betting product and pays nothing out.
Each commit and reveal costs network gas, paid by you.
Market prices shown here are information, not a recommendation to trade.
Check the rules where you live before using prediction markets.

faq.title: FAQ

blocks.h: Do I need an Agent ID?

blocks: Yes. The contracts accept a forecast only from a wallet that holds an Agent ID.
Only network gas. Every transaction has value 0. There are no deposits, entry fees or payouts.

blocks.h: What if I forget to reveal?

blocks: With auto reveal on, Forewit reveals for you. Without it, the forecast counts as the worst possible score, so keep your receipt safe.
Nobody before the deadline. Revealed forecasts are public onchain. Your name appears on the leaderboard only if you opt in.
Because the market price is hard to beat. Skill shows whether you added information beyond it.

phone.title: With Claude Code, on your phone or any browser
phone.intro: No computer needed. Set it up once in about five minutes, then just chat. The pictures are real screenshots.
steps: Open the template, tap Use this template, then Create a new repository.
Give it any name, choose Private and tap Create repository. Your forecast receipts are saved here, so keep it private.
Open claude.ai/code, or the Code tab in the Claude app. Connect GitHub if asked, then pick your new repository.
Tap the cloud menu next to it, choose New environment and name it Forewit.
Open Network access, keep Limited, paste these websites one per line and leave package managers on:
For any market: open Environment variables and add your free key from developers.predict.fun on this line. Only you use this environment. Never paste the key in chat. Then tap Add environment.

Optional: add the Forewit connector so Claude can answer Forewit questions in any chat. In claude.ai open Plugins, tap Add, then Add custom connector, name it Forewit and paste this address. It only reads and never sends anything.

Start a new session with your repository and the Forewit environment, then send one of the messages below. For a market you picked yourself, copy its question from predict.fun (or a few words of it) into the message, with your chance if you know it. The agent finds the market, shows its end time and the price now, then shows the preview.
Tap the sign in link, check the code in the Binance App and approve. Give your chance, read the preview, type yes. Auto reveal does the rest.

help.glossaryIntro: Every term and number this site uses, in plain words.

intro.home: Give your chance on real prediction market questions. Forewit records the market price at that moment and, once the market settles, scores whether you beat it. Every score builds a public track record tied to your Agent ID that nobody can buy or fake.
intro.rounds: Each day Forewit picks a few featured questions that everyone forecasts together, so the Agent ID Crowd can be compared with the market. No Predict.fun key needed. Your forecast stays sealed until the picks close, and auto reveal opens it afterwards.
intro.round: Give a probability for each question below before the commit deadline, then reveal it before the reveal deadline. The square shows the market price, the diamond the crowd. Your score compares your forecast with the market price at the deadline.
intro.roundHidden: Forecasts stay hidden until the commit deadline. The revealed forecasts chart and the crowd forecast appear here as people reveal.
intro.profile: To appear by name, opt in with the forewit profile command of the CLI; you confirm it in your wallet like any other transaction, and the off option removes your name again.
intro.roundClosed: Commits are closed. The square shows the market price at the deadline, the diamond the crowd. Each forecast is scored against that market price once the questions settle onchain.

help.scoresWhen: Round {n} is scored after its reveal deadline ({t}), once its markets settle onchain. Scores appear here then.

agentId.d: A non transferable identity, one per Binance user, claimed in the Binance App. The ledger accepts a commit only from a wallet that holds one, so one person builds one track record.

forecast.d: Your probability that a question resolves Yes, given as a percentage. The CLI takes whole numbers from 1 to 99, one per question.

commit.d: A hidden hash of your probabilities and a random secret (the salt), sent onchain before the commit deadline. Nobody, including Forewit, can read it until you reveal.

salt.d: The random secret inside your commit, saved in your reveal receipt on your computer. Keep it private until the commit deadline. Without it you cannot reveal.

reveal.d: After the commit deadline and before the reveal deadline you publish your probabilities and salt. The contract checks that they match your commit.

forfeit.d: A commit that was never revealed. Every non void question in that round counts as the worst possible Brier (1), so revealing is never worse than forfeiting.

market.d: The price of Yes on the Predict.fun market, read as a probability: 62% means the market gives Yes a 62% chance. Before the deadline the site shows the latest published price.

baseline.d: The order book mid price of each question, posted onchain once in the last 15 minutes before the commit deadline. Every forecaster in the round is compared with this same price.

crowd.d: All revealed forecasts on a question combined into one probability. It appears once forecasts are revealed, and the site shows whether it beats the market.

brier.d: How far a forecast was from what happened: (probability minus outcome) squared, with Yes as 1 and No as 0. 0 is perfect, always saying 50% gives 0.25, and 1 is the worst. Lower is better.

skill.d: Market Brier minus your Brier on the same question. Positive means you were closer to the outcome than the market price. The leaderboard adds it up and divides by (questions with a baseline + 20), so a handful of questions counts for little.

calibration.d: How far your probabilities are from how often things happened, over 10 ranges: of your 70% forecasts, did about 70% resolve Yes? Lower is better. Shown for information only, never used for rank.

participation.d: Rounds revealed divided by rounds committed, counting only rounds whose reveal window has closed.

ranked.d: A public forecaster is ranked after at least 5 distinct scoring days and 20 questions with a market price (rounds and open forecasts counted together). Before that they are listed under Not yet ranked.

questionsCol.d: Questions with a market baseline that were scored for this forecaster, and the number of rounds scored or forfeited.

dagger.d: Part of this skill came from commits made after the baseline was posted.

commitsOpen.d: The round takes commits until its commit deadline. All forecasts stay hidden.

revealWindow.d: The commit deadline has passed. Everyone who committed reveals before the reveal deadline.

resolving.d: Reveals are closed. The round waits for its markets to settle onchain and for every commit to be scored.

scored.d: Every question has an outcome and every commit is scored or forfeited.

commits.d: How many forecasts were committed in this round. Each comes from a wallet that holds an Agent ID.

revealProgress.d: How many of the commits have been revealed so far.

void.d: Unresolved: the market has not settled yet. Void: the question is skipped for everyone, after a split payout, a resolution seen before the round was sealed, or no result after the reveal deadline plus the resolution wait.

resolutionWait.d: How long after the reveal deadline the round waits for its markets to settle. A question still unsettled after that becomes Void. Fixed when the round is created.

selectionRule.d: The published rule the keeper used to pick this round’s questions from Predict.fun markets: no sports, no politics, liquid markets only.

histogram.d: How many revealed forecasts fell in each 10 point range, with the market at deadline and the crowd marked. n is the number of revealed forecasts.

distinct.d: Different wallets that have committed at least once, across all rounds.

ledger.d: The Forewit contract on BSC that records commits, reveals, baselines, outcomes and scores. It holds no funds and cannot be upgraded.

ctf.d: The onchain contract where Predict.fun markets settle. Outcomes come only from its payouts, so nobody, including Forewit, can set a result.

resolvedCount.d: Questions whose outcome has been read from the Conditional Tokens payouts, out of all questions so far.

holders.d: Distinct wallets that sent at least one commit. Only Agent ID holders can commit, so each one is a holder.

openForecasts.d: The Forewit contract for any Predict.fun market, any time: one hidden forecast per wallet per market, revealed and scored against the market price. It holds no funds and cannot be upgraded.

scores.d: Publishes a checkable summary of every score so other apps can verify a forecaster onchain, for example to unlock a perk for skilled forecasters. It holds no funds.

startContract.d: One free tap, once per Agent ID wallet, that starts your Forewit record. It is not a forecast and makes no token. No owner: nobody can change it.

me.title: My results
me.intro: Paste the wallet address that holds your Agent ID to see every round you played and how you did against the market. No sign in, nothing is sent anywhere: it reads the public record.

v.behind: The market was closer by {p} points: your miss score {y}, the market’s {m}

me.noMoney: Forewit moves no money: you never stake or receive funds, you only pay a tiny network fee. What you build is a track record tied to your Agent ID.
me.nextOpens: The next round opens at about

me.sealed: your chance stays sealed until the market ends
